{{nihongo|'''Ōmunaji Shrine'''|大穴持神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōsumi Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The current deities enshrined are as follows. </ref><ref name="Kirishima City Explanation Board">Explanation board in the precincts (installed by Kirishima City Board of Education). </ref>.
; Main enshrined deity
:* '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Okuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Oomi Takamikoto}}''' (Onanji no Mikoto/Onamuchi no Mikoto, Okuninushi no Mikoto)
; Aidenjin
:* {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona Mikoto}}
:* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ootoshigami}} (Otoshigami, Ootoshigami)
:* {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Okami}}
:* Kirishima Okami - Moved and enshrined in {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}}22 ({{ill|1947|Q5263|qid=Q5263}} from the current site of Hirose Community Center).The theory that the personal deity of the enshrined deity is compared to Onamuchi (Ookuninushi) is based on the 9th year of {{ill|Hōki|Q18520676|qid=Q18520676}} of {{ill|Nara period|Q189178|qid=Q189178}} ({{ill|778|Q30452|qid=Q30452}}, and it can be seen as ``Oanamochi Shrine'' in ``{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}'' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}. It is sometimes introduced as a shrine that shows that the Okuninushi faith, which originated in the Izumo region, extends to Kagoshima.<ref>[https://www.nhk.or.jp/special/detail/20140102.html NHK Special "Series Sengu Part 2 Izumo Taisha - The Mystery of the Okuninushi"] NHK, first broadcast on January 2, 2014. </ref>. Currently, he is worshiped as a god of medicine and a god of vipers.<ref name="Kirishima City Explanation Board"/>

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
Its founding date is unknown<ref name="Shrine Agency"/>. According to the company records, it was founded in the {{ill|Tenpyō|br|Tenpyō|ca|Era Tenpyō|de|Tempyō|es|Tenpyō|fa|تنپیو|fr|Ère Tenpyō|ia|Tenpyo|id|Tempyō|it|Tenpyō|ja|天平|ko|덴표|no|Tenpyō|pt|Tenpyō|ru|Тэмпё|simple|Tenpyō|sr|Тенпјо|tr|Tenpyō|uk|Темпьо (ненґо)|zh|天平 (日本)|zh_yue|天平 (日本)|qid=Q1199879}} years ({{ill|729|Q23561|qid=Q23561|lt=729}}-{{ill|749|Q23624|qid=Q23624}}) {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine Journal Articles|1912}}. It was originally enshrined on a divine island (Miyazu, Miyazu), which will be mentioned later, but there is a legend that it was relocated to its current location due to the collapse of the island.

In "Kokubu Shokoki" and "Shrines and Temples", it is said that it was originally enshrined in Mt. Tsugaru, Oshu, {{ill|Hyūga Province|Q513737|qid=Q513737}} Kushijima, {{ill|Ōsumi Province|Q981002|qid=Q981002}}Fukusenowatari passed through Fukushima Village and was enshrined here in Komura.{{Sfn|Oanamochi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}<ref name="Shrine Agency"/>.

=== Outline ===
In "{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}", the ancient Oanamochi Shrine appears as follows {{Sfn|Oanamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1998}}.
* {{ill|Tenpyō-hōji|Q1346307|qid=Q1346307}} December 8 ({{ill|764|Q31163|qid=Q31163}}) Koretsukijo - Three islands appeared due to an eruption that occurred at the border between Osumi Province and {{ill|Satsuma Province|Q667475|qid=Q667475}}.
* {{ill|Tenpyō-jingo|Q1373181|qid=Q1373181}} 2nd year ({{ill|766|Q30564|qid=Q30564}}) June 5th article - ``Osumi no Kuni no Kami'' built Niijima and the tremors continued, and many of the people were exiled, so he donated things and saved them.
* {{ill|Hōki|Q18520676|qid=Q18520676}}9th year ({{ill|778|Q30452|qid=Q30452}}) December 12th article - The name of the god who created the island during the Jingo era was ``Oanamochigami,'' and it was made into a government shrine.
The prevailing theory was that the three islands that appeared were Heda-kojima, Benten-jima, and Oki-kojima off the coast of Hayato Port {{Sfn|Oanamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1998}}. However, volcanically, it is said that they were not caused by eruptions during the Nara period, and there is a theory that the three islands were actually located near {{ill|Sakurajima|Q128841|qid=Q128841}}, but were later submerged under the sea {{Sfn|Oanamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1998}}.

It is also said that this divine island (Miyasu, Miyazu) has a rapid called Miyase on the left side of the shore of the Amori River, so it may have been submerged under water and became the current rapid.In addition to this, the ``''Hachiman Usamiya Imperial Trust Senshu'''' states that an island created under the sea in Osumi due to volcanic activity was named ``Kagoshima'' in {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Q1373049|qid=Q1373049}}2 ({{ill|768|Q29961|qid=Q29961}}).

{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{ill|Q1106493 2|qid=Q1106493 2|lt=In the Shinmeicho}}, ``Ōanamochi Shrine'' is listed in Osumi Province {{ill|Soo District, Kagoshima|Q1043870|qid=Q1043870|lt=囎唹 District}}, and it is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi Shrine}} {{Sfn|Ōanamochi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}.

Regarding the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} period, the ``Ishizuki Jiyaku Shosha'' dated 2nd year {{ill|Kenji (era)|Q1327993|qid=Q1327993}} ({{ill|1276|Q5530|qid=Q5530}}) states that ``Great It is written as ``Anamochi Nitta Gotan'', and it appears that {{ill|Gokenin|Q63765|qid=Q63765}} ``Princess Tayu Atsuki (□ is omitted)'' served as the chief priest.{{Sfn|Ōanamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1998}}.In the {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} period, 3 to 3 sho 3 go {{Sfn|Oanamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1998}} (or 3 to 5 sho 5 go {{ Sfn|Meiji Shrine Journal Fee|1912}}), and the Taniguchi family has been in charge of the shrine family from that time to the present {{Sfn|Oanamochi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1998}}. In addition, ``{{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}}'' 14th year ({{ill|1843|Q7629|qid=Q7629}}) depicts the precincts at that time, and it is known that the sea stretched out in front of the torii gate<ref name="Oanamochi Shrine Explanation Board"/>.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, May 4th year of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} ({{ill|1871|Q7746|qid=Q7746}}), it was listed as a {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=prefectural shrine|qid=Q90139226}} in the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.

=== Setsusha ===
There are the following five shrines within the precincts <ref name="Oanamochi Shrine Explanation Board"/>.
*Nittengu Shrine
* Inari Shrine
* Moon Heaven Palace
* Otamiya
* Great Royal Palace
These five shrines are also depicted in the "Sangoku Scenic Spots Zue" and are enshrined in almost the same location as they are today <ref name="Oanamochi Shrine Explanation Board"/>.
